mechanism: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 integrase inhibitor
note: HIV-1 integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (raltegravir 2007; dolutegravir, bictegravir, cabotegravir) were carried by cell-culture replication assays with a protein-adjusted IC95/IC90 trough target, one SHIV-macaque proof of concept and standard rat/rabbit/dog toxicology; no humanized-mouse model was on the critical path.
label: HIV-1 integrase inhibitors

engagement.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) with in-vitro resistance selection
engagement.note: Diketo-acid strand-transfer inhibitors blocked HIV-1 replication in cells by inhibiting integration; the cell assay became the class's target-engagement model.
engagement.short: Diketo acids block integration in cells
engagement.quote: In this report, we describe diketo acid inhibitors of HIV-1 integrase that manifest antiviral activity as a consequence of their effect on integration.
engagement.judgement: Model opens with the first class-defining cell-culture paper (diketo acids L-731,988/L-708,906, class proxies). model_filed=true because the Isentress label section 12.4 reports cell-culture antiviral activity and cell-culture-selected resistance for raltegravir.

engagement.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) with in-vitro resistance selection
engagement.note: In BENCHMRK, 68% of raltegravir failures carried integrase mutations (Q148, N155) already known from cell-culture/phenotypic resistance work: the drug acts on integrase in patients.
engagement.quote: Integrase mutations known to be associated with phenotypic resistance to raltegravir arose during treatment in 64 patients (68%).
engagement.reason: Resistance maps to integrase in patients
engagement.judgement: Engagement read as target-specific proof: resistance in patients maps to integrase positions. The model side (mutations 'evolved either in cell culture or in subjects treated with raltegravir', Q148/N155, later Y143) is the Isentress label section 12.4 (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=89a5ec53-d956-4329-8004-0f40f51c88a3); Cooper 2008 supplies the patient side, so comparison_stated=false. Monotherapy viral-load decline (Markowitz 2006) was assigned to dose/efficacy rather than reused here.

dose.model: Cell-culture IC95 in 50% human serum (protein-adjusted) as the plasma-trough target
dose.note: Cell-culture potency was the only exposure yardstick; the serum-adjusted IC95 trough target was formalised for raltegravir.
dose.short: Cell IC95 is the trough target
dose.quote: The antiviral activity of these compounds is due exclusively to inhibition of one of the two catalytic functions of integrase, strand transfer.
dose.judgement: The protein-adjusted IC95/IC90 trough target is a derivative of the same cell assay, so the strip opens in 2000 with the class-defining cell paper rather than the first raltegravir PK paper.

dose.model: Cell-culture IC95 in 50% human serum (protein-adjusted) as the plasma-trough target
dose.note: Raltegravir troughs at all four doses exceeded the cell IC95 (33 nM) and all cut HIV RNA >=1.7 log10; target held, no dose ranking.
dose.short: Troughs above IC95; all doses worked
dose.quote: Mean trough MK-0518 concentrations at each dose exceeded the IC95 of 33 nM.
dose.reason: Trough above IC95 held in patients
dose.judgement: Called 'same' because every dose with trough > IC95 was active; the trial never tested exposures below the target, so the model could not rank 100-600 mg BID (magnitude=direction_only). Later consistent evidence not added as a new entry: once-daily 800 mg with ~6-fold lower troughs was inferior in QDMRK (Eron 2011, 10.1016/S1473-3099(11)70196-7; Rizk 2012, 10.1128/AAC.06417-11). Registry record for Protocol 004 not located; registry_date null.

efficacy.note: Cell-culture replication was the efficacy model; a SHIV-macaque proof of concept with class proxy L-870812 followed in 2004.
efficacy.quote: In this report, we describe diketo acid inhibitors of HIV-1 integrase that manifest antiviral activity as a consequence of their effect on integration.
efficacy.judgement: Cell culture, not the macaque, is the model the class relied on (FDA microbiology basis). The SHIV-macaque study (Hazuda 2004, 10.1126/science.1098632) dosed L-870812, a class proxy, and no source compares it with patient outcomes, so it is noted but not given its own strip.

efficacy.note: Ten days of raltegravir monotherapy cut HIV RNA 1.7-2.2 log10 and took >=50% of patients below 400 copies/mL, as the cell assay predicted.
efficacy.quote: MK-0518 showed potent antiretroviral activity as short-term monotherapy and was generally well tolerated at all doses.
efficacy.reason: Viremia fell as cell assay predicted
efficacy.judgement: The cell assay predicts antiviral activity, not a clinical effect size, so magnitude=direction_only. Durable suppression in triple-class-resistant patients (Steigbigel 2008, 10.1056/NEJMoa0708975) is consistent but makes no model comparison and is not a status change. No integrase inhibitor failed in patients for efficacy, so 'neg' is unavailable.

safety.model: Rat and rabbit embryo-fetal development studies (plus rat/dog chronic toxicology)
safety.note: Raltegravir's label records rat and rabbit embryo-fetal studies without adverse developmental outcomes; no patient comparison existed.
safety.quote: No embryo/fetal effects were noted up to the highest dose of 1000 mg/kg/day.
safety.confidence: medium: quote taken from the current DailyMed label (revised 5/2022); the 2007 original was not checked
safety.judgement: Year is the raltegravir approval (NDA 022145, 2007), the first time the class's tox package was filed; the quoted sentence is the rabbit study. Earlier class compounds (L-870810, S-1360) were stopped on preclinical or PK grounds before any patient comparison.

safety.model: Rat and rabbit embryo-fetal development studies (plus rat/dog chronic toxicology)
safety.note: Dolutegravir's rat/rabbit studies were negative (rabbit exposure below human), yet Tsepamo found neural-tube defects in 0.30% of conception exposures vs 0.10% on other ART.
safety.quote: The prevalence of neural-tube defects was higher in association with dolutegravir treatment at conception than with non-dolutegravir ART at conception (difference, 0.20 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.01 to 0.59) or with other types of ART exposure.
safety.judgement: Model side is the Tivicay label section 8.1 Animal Data ('No adverse effects on embryo-fetal (rats and rabbits) or pre/postnatal (rats) development were observed at up to the highest dose tested'; rat exposure ~27x human, rabbit below human), https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=63df5af3-b8ac-4e76-9830-2dbb340af922; the label juxtaposes it with the Botswana human data. The signal was first published in a 2018 NEJM letter (Zash 2018, 10.1056/NEJMc1807653, verified on PubMed but paywalled and unquotable), so the entry is dated to the 2019 full report. Status follows the 2019 comparison per rule 5; the current label's larger cohort (>9,460 conception exposures) reports 0.11% (95% CI 0.05-0.19%), i.e. the signal later attenuated toward background, which a re-score may weigh. Tsepamo is observational surveillance, so registry_date is null.
